## Natural history notes

A small longtail skipper characterized by brown wings, pale translucent spots on the forewings, and long tail-like extensions on the hindwings. In Florida, it is found in sunny open habitats such as fields, roadsides, gardens, parks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, and disturbed areas where legumes and nectar plants are available. Adults feed on nectar from low flowers, while the caterpillars feed on plants in the pea family, often using folded or tied leaves as shelters during development.
